lesson_title: One Third and a Hidden Triangle: Cones, Pyramids, Spheres
hook_text: Fill the cone. Pour. Fill again. Pour. One more — EXACTLY three fills every time.
clip_script: That one third is not folklore — it is a laboratory fact. Take a hollow cone and a hollow cylinder of matching base and height, fill the cone with water, and pour. Three pours fill the cylinder. Always exactly three. Run the square pyramid: base edge twelve centimetres, perpendicular height eight. Base area: one hundred and forty-four. Volume: one third times one hundred and forty-four times eight — three hundred and eighty-four cubic centimetres.
visual_style: Water pouring from a glowing cone into a cylinder in three satisfying tips, a counter ticking one-two-three, then the one-third formula assembling over a pyramid wireframe.
mood: Science-experiment wonder with a clean numerical payoff.
pacing: Three deliberate pour beats, then a quick confident run through the pyramid numbers.
